sentences.text:
1 The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.260/2012 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Vatakara, is the appellant herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).

2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Sections 140 and 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 05.01.2012.

According to the petitioner, on 05.01.2012 at about 7 p.m., while he was walking along the road from Kallode to Perambra, a motorcycle bearing reg.no.KL-56-A- 2761 driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down and as a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the driver cum owner and the 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.18,00,000/-.

4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the 2025:KER:30650 MACA NO.2604 OF 2017 driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A17 and C1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.4,73,386/- rounded to Rs.4,73,390/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
9.

Heard Sri.V.N. Ramesan Nambisan, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant,
and Smt. M.Meena John, the learned Standing Counsel for the 2nd respondent.
10. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.

According to him, the petitioner was 2025:KER:30650 MACA NO.2604 OF 2017 working as Driver, getting a daily income of Rs.750/-,
but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.12000/-.
According to the learned counsel, the notional income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

On the other hand,
the learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the notional income of the petitioner as fixed by Balan Nair vs New India Assurance Company Limited on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183968418/

11. As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2012 will come to Rs.8500/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the decision in Yoosaf N.K. Vs. Managing Director, Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (MACA No.289/2016), the notional income of a driver involved in an accident in the year 2012 was fixed by this Court at Rs.12000/-.

entities.text: Yoosaf N.K. Vs. Managing Director, Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (MACA No.289/2016)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the absence of any evidence to the contrary, the notional income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal appears to be reasonable and hence does not call for any interference.

12. In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
1. Multiple (4-5) abrasion of 1x2 cm size over left side of forehead.
2. Multiple abrasions of 1x2 cm size over left side of forearm.
3. Traumatic optic neuropathy due to fracture of orbital wall, 2025:KER:30650 MACA NO.2604 OF 2017 4.
Lacerated wound of 1x1x1 cm size over left eyebrow.
5. Lacerated wound of 1x1x1 cm size over forehead.
6. Severe lid edema & Echymosia left side.
7. Fracture left orbital wall preseptal emphysema.
8. Fracture nasal bone.

9. Fracture left sygometic archanoid.
10.
Nasal septum deviated to right.
11. Lacerated wound on hip.

12. Loss of vision left eye and vision power completely and permanently disabled.
13.
From Ext.C1 disability certificate it is revealed that because of the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner lost eye sight of the left eye.
Because of the above fact, his permanent physical disability was assessed as 30% by the medical board.

According to the learned counsel, since the petitioner was a heavy vehicle driver, and in the accident he lost sight of left eye, he could not continue his job as a driver and as such his functional disability is to be taken as 100%.

On the other hand,
the learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the permanent physical Balan Nair vs New India Assurance Company Limited on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183968418/
3 disability of the petitioner as fixed by the medical board does not call for any interference.
14.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The fact that the petitioner is a heavy vehicle driver is not in dispute.
Ext.A17 driving license produced by the petitioner will prove the same.
After the injuries sustained in the accident he could not continue his job 2025:KER:30650 MACA NO.2604 OF 2017 as driver.
He may be able to do some other work but he could not hereafter continue to work as a driver.
Therefore the functional disability of the petitioner will be much more than what is assessed by the medical board.
Considering the entire facts, I hold that his functional disability can be fixed at 50%.
15. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 57 years.

Therefore, 10% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v.
Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 9, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

sentences.text:
In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.7,12,800/-.
16.
Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.48000/- being the income for 4 months @Rs.12000/-.
Considering the nature of the injuries sustained and the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner might have lost income at least for a period of 8 months.

Therefore, towards 'loss of income' the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs.96000/- (
12000 x 8 months).
17. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.15000/-.
Towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.10000/- was 2025:KER:30650 MACA NO.2604 OF 2017 awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
No amount was awarded for extra nourishment.
18. The petitioner sustained serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 9 days.
Because of the injuries sustained, he lost the vision of left eye.

Considering the injuries, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings' and 'loss of amenities of life' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.75000/- and Rs.1,50,000/-
respectively.

20. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.10,50,386/-,
